title: A True Guru Guides Us From Experience | Sri Daya Mata

# A True Guru Guides Us From Experience

### By Sri Daya Mata

*A spiritual discourse inspired by the teachings of Paramahansa Yogananda, presented by Self-Realization Fellowship / Yogoda Satsanga Society of India.*

---

### The Sacred Awakening of the Soul

In the quiet sanctuary of our souls, there is a deep, unspoken longing that cannot be satisfied by any worldly possession, relationship, or intellectual accomplishment. This inner ache is the soul’s memory of its divine origin, a gentle but persistent calling from the Divine Mother, urging us to return to Her eternal embrace. In our seeking, we often wander through the labyrinth of worldly experiences, trying to satisfy this spiritual hunger with temporary pleasures. 

However, there comes a time in the incarnation of every seeker when the heart cries out with absolute sincerity for something real, something permanent. It is in response to this earnest, heartfelt cry that the Infinite Lord sends a true Guru, or Sadguru, into the seeker’s life. Sri Daya Mata, the beloved third president of Self-Realization Fellowship, reminds us that the appearance of the Guru is not a matter of chance; it is a direct response from the Divine to the soul’s sincere yearning for liberation.

### What is a True Sadguru?

A true Guru is not merely a spiritual teacher who has studied the scriptures or mastered intellectual philosophies. A teacher may impart knowledge, but only a Guru can impart life. A true Guru is a living channel of the Divine, one who has fully traversed the arduous path to God-realization, dissolved his ego in the ocean of Cosmic Consciousness, and returned to the shore of mortal existence solely to guide other seeking souls back Home.

Sri Daya Mata recalls how her beloved Guru, Paramahansa Yogananda, embodied this spiritual state of perfect realization. He did not speak to His disciples from theories or dogmatic beliefs. Every word He uttered, every piece of guidance He offered, was born of His direct, unmediated experience of the Divine Presence.

> "The Guru is the living embodiment of God’s love and wisdom on earth. He does not ask us to follow blindly, but rather invitationally says, 'Come, experience what I have experienced. Walk this path with me, and you shall behold the same Light that I behold.'"

### Guidance Born of Direct Experience

When we are guided by one who speaks from direct experience, our spiritual journey undergoes a profound transformation. In the spiritual life, doubts and obstacles are inevitable. The mind becomes restless, the ego rebels, and the delusions of Maya try to pull us back into the world of dualities. During these times of trial, the intellectual concepts we have gathered from books often fail to sustain us. We need a hand to hold in the dark—a hand that is strong, steady, and anchored in the Unchangeable Reality.

Paramahansa Yogananda often told His disciples that the Guru’s primary role is to act as a mirror, reflecting the disciple's true nature as an immortal spark of the Divine, while gently pointing out the spots of egoic delusion that must be cleansed. Because the Guru has already conquered the delusions of this world, He knows every trap, every bypass, and every illusion that the disciple will encounter. His guidance is uniquely tailored to the individual needs of each soul.

> "Do not look to me as a person," Gurudeva would say to us. "Look to the One who sent me. Let your mind be absorbed in the love of the Divine Mother, for Whom my heart beats with every breath. I am only Her servant, sent to show you the way to Her feet."

### The Alchemy of Divine Discipline

To be guided by a true Guru requires a willing heart and a surrender of the ego. This is often the most challenging aspect of the disciple-guru relationship. The ego clings desperately to its habits, its opinions, and its self-will. When the Guru points out our flaws or guides us in a direction that opposes our personal desires, we may experience inner resistance.

Sri Daya Mata teaches us that the discipline of the Guru is never born of anger or a desire to control. It is the purest expression of divine love. Just as a jeweler must cut and polish a rough stone to reveal the brilliant diamond hidden within, so does the Guru use the tools of loving discipline to polish the disciple’s consciousness. 

Through this process, the disciple learns the invaluable lesson of attunement. By aligning our limited human will with the wisdom-guided will of the Guru, we gradually dissolve the barriers of ego and open ourselves to the unobstructed flow of God’s grace.

### Five Practical Spiritual Habits for Attuning with the Guru

To experience the active guidance of the Guru in our daily lives, Sri Daya Mata encourages us to cultivate specific spiritual habits that foster deep inner attunement:

*   **Daily, Devotional Meditation:** Do not let your meditation become mechanical. Begin each practice by mentally bowing at the feet of the Guru, praying deeply: "Lord, guide my thoughts. Gurudeva, breathe through me, love through me, meditate through me."
*   **The Practice of the Presence of God:** Throughout the busy hours of the day, keep a silent current of devotion running in the background of your mind. Mentally talk to the Guru as you would to your dearest, most intimate friend.
*   **Cultivate Selfless Service (Seva):** Perform your daily duties with the attitude of offering. When we serve others without selfish motives, we align our hearts with the universal love of the Guru, who lives only to serve humanity.
*   **Study the Sacred Writings with Devotion:** Spend time daily reading the words of Gurudeva. Do not read merely for intellectual stimulation, but let His words sink deep into your heart, allowing His spiritual vibration to elevate your consciousness.
*   **Willing Obedience to Spiritual Laws:** Apply the Guru's teachings practically in your life. Practice truthfulness, kindness, self-control, and above all, love for all beings. True attunement is demonstrated through our actions.

### The Living Presence Beyond the Physical Form

One of the greatest reassurances Sri Daya Mata offers to seekers is that the connection between Guru and disciple is not bound by time, space, or physical presence. Even after a great master leaves his physical body, his spiritual influence, his love, and his guidance remain fully accessible to every disciple who tunes in with love and devotion.

When we sit in the silence of deep meditation, practicing the sacred techniques of Kriya Yoga taught by our Gurudeva, we transcend the limitations of the material world. In that sacred interior silence, we find that the Guru is closer to us than our very breath. He is not far away in some distant realm; He is seated on the altar of our own hearts, waiting for us to turn our attention away from the clamor of the world and rest in His peace.

### A Closing Prayer for Divine Attunement

Let us close our eyes for a moment, take a deep breath, and draw our attention to the spiritual eye between the brows. Let us pray together in the depths of our hearts:

> "O Divine Mother, Heavenly Father, Beloved Gurudeva Paramahansa Yogananda! Teach me to tune my restless mind to Thy silent voice of peace. Take away my self-will and replace it with Thy divine, wisdom-guided will. Help me to surrender my ego at Thy holy feet. May Thy love shine through my eyes, Thy strength manifest through my actions, and Thy joy overflow in my soul. Guide me from the darkness of ignorance to the eternal light of Thy presence, now and forevermore."

*Jai Guru. Jai Ma.*
